memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"So God led the people around by the desert road toward the Red Sea. The
Israelites went up out of Egypt ready for battle." - Ex 13:18 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is a lovely detail. God routes them away from war, and yet they march out
"ready for battle," in ordered ranks.

Both things are true at once. God spared them a fight they were not ready for,
and He still brought them out prepared. His protection did not make them passive.

That balance is worth holding. Some believers assume that if God is sovereign,
preparation does not matter. Others live as though everything depends on their
readiness. Scripture keeps both. Paul tells the Ephesians to put on the full
armour of God, and then reminds them that the battle belongs to the Lord and the
strength is His (Eph 6:10-11).

Notice also where God leads them: "toward the Red Sea." From a human standpoint
this looks like the worst possible direction. Ahead lies water they cannot
cross, and behind them, soon, an army. God leads them into an impossible place
on purpose.

Sometimes God's guidance takes us somewhere that makes no sense until we see
what He intends to do there. The Red Sea was not an obstacle God failed to
anticipate. It was the stage He had chosen.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you preparing faithfully while trusting God for the outcome?
2. Has God led you somewhere that looks like a dead end?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, help me to prepare well and trust You completely. When You lead me to
impossible places, remind me that You chose the ground. Amen.
